rv.q: Frances Hodgson Burnett novel that served as the source material for Marsha Norman's script. If you never read the book as a kid, the story involves a young girl who, following the death of her parents, is taken to a creepy Yorkshire manor house run by two rival brothers, one of whom is mourning his lost wife and another who is up to no good.

And with a little luck, their production of the Tony award-winning THE SECRET GARDEN won’t stay a secret for long. In keeping with the British holiday tradition of sharing ghost stories, this timeless and enchanting, show with more than a few ghosts is a holiday treat.
Its operatic score is gorgeously sung by a cast as talented as patrons will find on any stage this season.
Theo Ubique's alluring production is a timeless tale that blooms with the power of love.
This new, thoughtful Theo production, directed by Christopher Pazdernik, makes a strong argument that 'The Secret Garden' should be revived more often.

Mary is a stubborn child who finds no meaning in anything until she discovers the secret garden and the key to unlock the door and bring it back to life. Make no mistake, this play is a musical with more singing than dialogue, 28 songs to be exact.
"The Secret Garden" is a surprisingly difficult story to tell, even with today's sensibilities and maturity. But at Theo, it has earned a respect as a marvelous holiday offering.
Theo’s solid staging of the novel’s musical adaptation (book and lyrics by Marsha Norman, score by Lucy Simon) reveals a tale that remains timeless.

Tonight, I was witness to the most beautiful production I have ever seen of "The Secret Garden" with a book and lyrics by Marsha Norman and music by Lucy Simon ( based on the novel by Frances Hodgson Burnett).
Make your holiday season and start to the New Year a lovely, memorable experience by not missing this little gem of wonderful theater.
